transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I’m not taking time away from patients who need it more. 

I guess what finally brought me in is... well, it’s a little hard to admit, especially being a social worker myself. I feel like I should know how to handle this. But I just feel like the part of me that used to reach out for people and, you know, really take pleasure in things has gone very quiet. 

I used to get so much joy out of my work, and my yoga classes, going to art galleries, even just journaling at the end of the day. And I’m still doing what I need to do—I don't want you to think I'm dropping the ball on my clients or anything—but lately, it just feels like I’m mostly moving through obligations. 

I feel a little silly even complaining about it, honestly. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
How long have you been noticing this loss of interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Well, let's see... I'd say it's been going on for about eight months? Give or take a little. It started right around the time we took my older relative into our apartment to live with us. 

Which, you know, is a good thing! I'm really glad we can be there to help, and I definitely don't want to sound like I'm complaining about family. I know how lucky we are. But I guess that's when this whole change in how I’m thinking and working, and... just connecting with people, really started to happen. 

Does eight months sound like a normal amount of time for something like this to build up? I just hope I haven't waited too long to finally bring it up to someone.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of low mood, low energy, or loss of interest like this at any other point in your life before these past eight months?

No, um... I really don't think I have. I've always been a pretty upbeat person, you know? Usually, I'm the one keeping the energy up for everyone else, especially at work and with my family. 

So this is... well, it's very new for me, just not feeling that spark at all. I haven't ever gone through a phase quite like this before these last few months. 

I mean, I hope that's a good thing? That I don't have a history of it, I mean. I guess it's probably better not to have felt this way before, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context for everything. Is that helpful for you to know?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over these past eight months—such as trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or sleeping much more or less than usual?

Um, actually, my sleep has been... pretty normal, I think. I mean, I still get my usual seven or eight hours a night. I might be a little more tired by the end of the day lately, but, well, with my relative moving in and just keeping up with work, I think anyone would be, right? I haven't had any real trouble falling asleep or waking up in the middle of the night or anything like that. 

I hope that's okay? I know in our field we always look at sleep as a big indicator for things, so I hope it doesn't make my other feelings seem... I don't know, less valid? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right pieces to the puzzle. But no, thankfully, my sleep is doing okay.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or being overly critical of yourself during these past eight months?

Oh, no... I don't think so. I mean, I really try hard not to get down on myself like that. Working in social work, you know, we're always encouraging our clients to be kind to themselves and practice self-compassion, so I try my best to practice what I preach. 

I haven't felt worthless or guilty or anything... maybe just a little stretched thin with the family changes and work, but that's just normal life stuff, right? I certainly don't hate myself or feel overly critical. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you an accurate picture. Is it a good sign that I'm not having those particular feelings? I really want to be as helpful as I can with your assessment.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate, focus, or make decisions, either at work or in daily life?

No, um... I think my focus has been pretty steady, honestly. 

I mean, with my caseload at work, I really have to stay sharp and make decisions for my clients every day, and I haven't dropped the ball there. I'm still keeping up with all my paperwork and everything, which takes a lot of concentration. 

Maybe every now and then I have to re-read an email if it's late in the afternoon, but... well, I think anyone would do that when they're a little tired, right? It's nothing out of the ordinary at all. 

So, no real changes there. I hope that helps rule some things out for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this all out. Am I answering these okay for you?
Over these past eight months, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually anxious, worried, or on edge, particularly in connection with the changes at home?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I've felt unusually anxious or on edge. I mean, sure, having a relative move in is an adjustment, and it can be a little stressful getting everyone settled into a new routine, but... well, it's nothing I can't handle. 

I really try to keep things peaceful at home and not let the little things get to me. I think I've been managing it all pretty well, actually. I certainly haven't been sitting around worrying all the time or feeling panicked. Just the normal day-to-day stuff, you know?

I hope it's okay that I'm not reporting a lot of anxiety? I know sometimes these things go hand in hand, but I really do feel like I'm keeping my head above water with the home situation. Does that sound like a normal response to you? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

When you notice this loss of interest and low mood, does it feel like it's mainly focused on thoughts and worries about your relative living with you and the changes at home, or do you feel this way pretty much throughout your day regardless of what you're doing or thinking about?

Um, well, I guess... I wouldn't say I have a low mood, really. And I'm definitely not losing interest in things. I mean, I still love my job and I care about my clients just as much as ever. 

If I'm ever feeling a little quiet or tired, it's usually just when I'm trying to figure out how to make things comfortable for everyone at home. You know, with my relative being there, I just want to make sure they feel welcome and that the house is running smoothly. So if I seem a bit distracted, it's really just focused on that—just wanting to be a good host and keep the peace. 

It definitely doesn't carry over into the rest of my day or affect my work or anything like that. I'm still very engaged with everything else. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just don't want you to think I'm walking around sad all day, because I'm really not. It's just a little extra responsibility at home, which is totally manageable. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay for you.
